reference.source: ILAE classification / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Classic Rett syndrome is caused by pathogenic variants in the X-linked MECP2 gene and occurs almost exclusively in girls
There is a period of apparently normal early development followed by regression, typically between six and eighteen months of age
Loss of purposeful hand use with characteristic midline hand stereotypies such as wringing and washing movements is a defining feature
Regression brings loss of acquired language, gait abnormalities or loss of ambulation, and deceleration of head growth causing acquired microcephaly
Epilepsy develops in a large proportion of patients, alongside breathing dysregulation, autonomic disturbance and scoliosis
Diagnosis rests on established clinical criteria supported by MECP2 genetic testing
Care is multidisciplinary and supportive, targeting seizures, feeding, orthopaedic and respiratory complications
reference.pathophysiology: Rett syndrome is caused by loss-of-function variants in MECP2, which encodes methyl-CpG-binding protein 2, a transcriptional regulator essential for mature neuronal function and synaptic maintenance. MeCP2 deficiency does not cause neurodegeneration but arrests and disrupts postnatal synaptic development and network refinement, so early milestones are attained and then lost. X-linkage and X-inactivation explain the female predominance and clinical variability, while the widespread neuronal dysfunction underlies the epilepsy, movement, breathing and autonomic manifestations.
additionalDifferentials: Neurodegenerative and metabolic disorders with regression
additionalInvestigations: MECP2 sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis, with wider gene testing if negative
EEG, which commonly shows epileptiform abnormalities and background slowing
Brain MRI to exclude alternative structural pathology
Assessment of growth and head circumference over time
Multidisciplinary evaluation of feeding, breathing, spine and development
redFlags: Developmental regression with loss of purposeful hand skills and language
Deceleration of head growth producing acquired microcephaly
New or worsening seizures superimposed on stereotyped movements
Progressive scoliosis or feeding and respiratory compromise
reference.prognosis: Rett syndrome causes lifelong severe disability with variable epilepsy, motor and communication impairment, but many individuals survive into adulthood with supportive care. Life expectancy is somewhat reduced, with cardiorespiratory complications and, less commonly, sudden death contributing to mortality.
pitfalls: Mistaking early regression for idiopathic autism and delaying MECP2 testing
Assuming a normal MECP2 result excludes a Rett-like disorder such as CDKL5 or FOXG1
Overtreating stereotypies as seizures without EEG correlation
Neglecting scoliosis, feeding and breathing complications that drive morbidity
management: Offer trofinetide, the approved disease-specific therapy, to reduce core symptom burden where available
Control epilepsy with anti-seizure medication tailored to the seizure type
Manage breathing dysregulation and autonomic disturbance, and monitor for QT prolongation with periodic ECG
Provide multidisciplinary physiotherapy, occupational therapy and orthotics, and surveil for scoliosis with bracing or spinal surgery as needed
Support feeding and nutrition, treating dysphagia and gastro-oesophageal reflux, with gastrostomy where required
Facilitate communication through augmentative and alternative communication and eye-gaze technology
Provide genetic counselling on the MECP2 variant and recurrence risk, with family testing
Monitor bone health given the increased fracture risk and coordinate lifelong supportive care
